about: Phase 7 (prompts/phase-07-analysis.md step 3, 'the point of the phase'): the two graphs `analysis::paths::tests` proves against. `defect` is a directed graph with one negative edge where Dijkstra finalises a node before its true shortest path (through the negative edge) is found — the exact defect SciGraphs's operator hides by always dispatching Dijkstra instead of the Bellman-Ford it also offers (docs/tutorials/panels/scigraphs/algorithms.qmd:74-75). `cycle` is a directed graph whose only path back to itself has negative total weight, which must be reported by name, not folded into a distance.

defect.dijkstra_is_wrong_because: b is finalised at cost 2 (direct edge) before c (cost 3) is even settled, so the c->b edge, though it would drop b to 1, never gets to relax it
defect.bellman_ford_is_correct_because: a->c->b costs 3 + (-2) = 1, less than the direct a->b edge's 2

cycle.expect: ShortestPaths::NegativeCycle naming every node of a, b, c (order not asserted past sorted membership — no duplicate, no ghost node), never a Distances(...) value
